newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude ends day mainly softer.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude ends day mainly softer.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil ended the day mainly softer but the prompt February contract bucked the trend to close just above its opening level.

The market was led down in late trade by NYMEX heating oil ahead of weekly statistics from the American Petroleum Institute (API), due after markets close, which are expected to show a build in distillate stocks, brokers said.

"It's come off the highs of the afternoon on the back of products in the U.S. which don't look very healthy - heating oil looks particularly weak. People expect a distillate build in the API's," one broker said.
February IPE Brent crude oil closed Tuesday up two cents at $24.58 a barrel, but March and April contracts lost some 11 and 16 cents respectively.
Initial trader estimates for the API covering the week ended January 3 were for a build of over one million barrels in distillate stocks.
The Brent Feb/Mar spread, which traded around +52/54 cents for most of the day, widened to +56 cents in late trade and in the last few minutes was doable at +60 cents, brokers said.
"The spread blew out on a combination of good outright Feb buying and good March selling. We should see a bit of a correction tomorrow," one commented.
January gas oil, which ended the day earlier down some $2.50 at $229.75 a tonne was called to open on Wednesday unchanged to $1 lower.
